- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: Galen Strawson's Basic Argument and constitutive luck: the parity problem for agent-causal self-formation
- **Output**: [[research/basic-argument-and-constitutive-luck-2026-10-25]]
- **Sources consulted**: 27. Full text: Strawson 1994 (JSTOR scan; every quote grep-verified with pages) and Nagel's "Moral Luck" (anthology reprint; pages not verified). Raw encyclopedia text: SEP Skepticism About Moral Responsibility §2.2–2.4, Free Will §3.1, Moral Luck and Moral Responsibility §2.2.2; IEP Moral Luck. Abstracts: Hartman 2018, Strawson 2000, O'Connor 2009, and chapters of Levy 2011, Kane 1996, Mele 1995/2006, Clarke 2003 and Pereboom 2001. Metadata only: Clarke 2005a, Istvan 2011, Kane 2000, Williams 1976/1981 and five others.
- **Verdict**: `recommended_action: article`. Target: `concepts/basic-argument-and-constitutive-luck` (367/370; 2 slots after the queued collapse-priority-problem; topics/ is the fallback).
  - The reactive-attitudes page is rejected as a fold host on scope: it is P.F.'s page and its disambiguation guard forbids it.
  - Every other host is at or near its length limit.
  - Scoping fixes are drafted with OLD at count 1: apex L155 (+4 of 10), moral-responsibility L79/L113/L173 (+8 of 12), moral-implications (+47 of 112). Integration passages are drafted for reactive-attitudes, source-versus-leeway, the rollback page and event-causal-libertarianism.
- **Key findings**:
  - Strawson made the parity point himself. His third response attacks "a certain picture of the self" independent of character: "whatever S decides, it decides as it does because of the way it is" (1994: 21). His n. 8 extends the demand to Kant's noumenal self. Dualism buys no exemption, though Strawson never names agent causation.
  - The agent-causal reply (Clarke 2003: 170–76, SEP-reported) rejects premise (2) rather than escaping the regress. It ends at the same primitive as the rollback; Levy's pincer and Strawson's two-horned S reply mark the junction.
  - Live defect in `moral-implications-of-genuine-agency` L72. "Independently identified" is false: Nagel's n. 3 says his paper was a reply to Williams. Nagel also named only "constitutive luck" (IEP).
  - The coiner of "constitutive luck" is unresolved: SEP says Nagel "named" it, IEP says he "probably gets [it] from Williams".
  - P-A5's "ultimate desert" residue is the Basic Argument's target. Flagged for /positions-evolve.

## 11:30 - research-voids
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: The retraction void. A mind can withdraw a belief and remember withdrawing it, yet cannot see where the withdrawn item is still doing inferential work. Readers who "had clearly recalled" a correction kept drawing inferences from the old information (Wilkes & Leatherbarrow 1988), and continued influence "occurs even if the retraction itself is well remembered" (Ecker et al. 2010). The philosophical frame is Harman's coherence theory, on which no ledger of reasons is kept (1984a/b; Godden 2012 dissents on rationality; Doyle 1992; Gärdenfors 1992; AGM 1985). The note covers four faces: individual (debriefing perseverance, Ross et al. 1975 and Anderson et al. 1980; continued influence, Johnson & Seifert 1994; the Chan et al. 2017 and Walter & Tukachinsky 2020 meta-analyses), formal (reason maintenance, Doyle 1979; the worst-case complexity of revision, Eiter & Gottlob via Gogic et al. 1998), machine (edited facts recalled while multi-hop consequences fail, Zhong et al. 2023 and Cohen et al. 2024) and community (retracted papers cited as valid, Budd et al. 1998, Hsiao & Schneider 2021, Schneider et al. 2020).
- **Category**: Mixed.
  - Principally Occluded at the readout (natural): the withdrawal is registered and the reliance is unmarked.
  - Unexplored as territory: it is measurable as the gap between recall of the correction and inference, and it is moved by process debriefing, causal alternatives and warnings.
  - Not Unexplorable: reason-maintenance architectures propagate retractions. The worst-case complexity residue for complete propagation is recorded and not claimed.
- **Output**: [[research/voids-retraction-void-2026-10-24]]. `recommended_action: article`, `target_slug: retraction-void` (slug free in obsidian/archive/hugo).

## 07:57 - research-voids
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: The template void. Every reader of minds starts from itself (egocentric anchoring and adjustment, Epley et al. 2004; false consensus that survives education and feedback, Krueger & Clement 1994). Where reader and read differ in architecture, the template misfits, and the misfit can be recorded as a property of the read mind, not as the reader's limit (an "exported void"). Faces: cross-cultural (Elfenbein & Ambady 2002 meta-analysis: in-group advantage, smaller with exposure, majority members poorer at reading minorities than the reverse; Matsumoto's comment and the reply), cross-neurotype (the double-empathy literature: Milton 2012; Edey et al. 2016; Sheppard et al. 2016; Crompton et al. 2020/2025) and cross-species/system (de Waal 1999 by paraphrase; Colombatto & Fleming 2024).
- **Category**: Mixed. Principally Unexplored: measurable from a third position, and exposure, incentives and disclosure all move it. The first-person readout is naturally Occluded: a misfit does not present as a limit. Not Unexplorable; the only unexplorable residue is the general other-minds asymmetry, owned by voids-between-minds.
- **Output**: [[research/voids-template-void-2026-10-23]]. `recommended_action: article`, `target_slug: template-void` (slug free in obsidian/archive/hugo). Fold fallback: ~130 words in `concepts/empathy` §"The Contemporary Three-Way Debate" (2,944/3,500). The voids neighbours are within 1–47 words of their hard limit. Per the driver brief, no voids article was created, no expand task was minted, `pending_articles` was NOT touched and todo.md was not edited. The candidate is for the open voids-slot NEEDS-HUMAN entry, alongside drift, cluelessness and luminosity.
- **Dedupe**: voids at 113/125 (`tools.evolution.state.count_section_files`). Zero hits in voids, research, topics/concepts/apex/positions/tenets, archive, reviews and workflow for "double empathy", Crompton, Sasson, Edey, Sheppard, DeBrabander, misattunement, Gernsbacher, Keysar, Nickerson, "egocentric anchoring", anthropodenial, Colombatto, Elfenbein, Ambady and "in-group advantage". The Epley, Krueger and "false consensus" hits are unrelated (read in context). Positive controls Fricker, Camerer and Schilbach hit where expected. Closest material: voids-between-minds (general asymmetry; the logomorphism sentence), boundary-and-projection (the success side of empathy), cross-state-void (state, not architecture) and conceptual-metabolism-void (knowledge imputation).
- **Key finding**: the displacement evidence is mixed, and the note says so. The 2025 *Nature Human Behaviour* registered report (N = 311) found no information-transfer difference between single- and mixed-neurotype chains, which fails to replicate 2020. Edey et al.'s failure is one-directional, not double. DeBrabander et al. 2019 found autistic raters share the negative trait impressions, so Sasson-type judgments are not template misfit. Livingston et al. 2025 (*Psychological Review*) and Fellowes 2026 (*JADD*) critique the construct; Kilgallon, Milton et al. 2026 restate it as sociological. The void rests on the robust egocentric literature plus the meta-analytic in-group advantage. Framework-independent: it fits Dualism without evidencing it. ## 10:12 - research-topic
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: Immediate emotions and the affect heuristic in choice
- **Output**: [[research/immediate-emotions-and-the-affect-heuristic-in-choice-2026-10-22]]
- **Sources consulted**: 40 cited.
  - Nine read in full text and grep-verified: Loewenstein et al. 2001 (OCR copy); Slovic et al. 2007; Pfister & Böhm 2008; Sokol-Hessner et al. 2009; Davis et al. 2009 (re-grepped); Many Labs 2; Garg et al. 2018; Jäger et al. 2020; the Schlösser 2009 dissertation.
  - The rest are Crossref/OpenAlex abstracts, plus three reused from today's affective-forecasting-gap fork (Schlösser 2013, Young 2019, Dorison 2019).
  - Not reached: Lerner et al. 2015 and Loewenstein & Lerner 2003 (abstract or opening text only).
- **Finding**:
  - Felt affect at choice is measured and predicts choice, but it is not manipulated, and it tracks value.
  - Incidental affect moves valuation (sadness → choice price, replicated, d ≈ 0.43) but not risk preference at scale (Dong et al. 2026, n = 7,000, preregistered, null). This is a partial hit, confined to the risk domain, on miswanting's own stated P-VS1 falsifier.
  - Rottenstreich & Hsee 2001 Study 1 reversed in Many Labs 2.
  - Lerner & Keltner 2001 replicated for risk judgement, not risk preference (Lu et al. 2026).
  - Integral and incidental affect are not interchangeable (Ferrer & Ellis 2021).
  - The affect heuristic's "affect" is "with or without consciousness". The literature fits P-VS1 without evidencing it. No band change.
- **Corrections to leads**:
  - Slovic 2002/2007 is one text (EJOR reprint of the *Heuristics and Biases* chapter).
  - The time-pressure study is Finucane's Study 1, though Slovic calls it the "second study".
  - The integral/incidental definitions are verified in Peters 2006 and Pham 2007, not Lerner 2015 (not reached).
- **Verdict**: article, `topics/immediate-emotions-and-the-affect-heuristic` (topics 357/370). A fold was infeasible: affective-forecasting-gap is at 3,789 (hard_warning), miswanting at 3,188, and value-in-selection has 2 words of headroom.

- **Status**: Success. This was a gap-closure run on the second-ranked banked note. No new void is proposed and no new file was created.

- **Measured first**: voids is **112/115** by `count_section_files`. With 3 slots and at least 8 banked candidates, a new note cannot win a slot and LIFO makes it net-negative, so this run followed the 10-10 precedent of strengthening rather than adding.
- **Key finding**: the fork is **historically occupied, not assembled, and not exclusive**:
  - Locke (*Essay* II.i.15 [raw]) states the cost accounting against Cartesian dualists in 1690: "whatever ideas the mind can receive and contemplate without the help of the body, it is reasonable to conclude it can retain without the help of the body too".
  - Descartes partitions the fork, with corporeal memory in the brain and intellectual memory in the soul (Joyce 1997 [raw, opening pages]).
  - Broad (1925 [raw], pp. 359–360) coins "mnemic persistents" for the dormant remainder: "we know nothing with certainty about the intrinsic nature of traces". He adds a fourth branch, a trace-carrier with "strong reason to doubt that it has the higher factors of mentality" (p. 651).
  - The sleep test case is the Locke–Leibniz "soul always thinks" dispute, which has the same structure as the 2018 persistent-activity vs activity-silent exchange (Constantinidis et al.; Lundqvist, Herman & Miller).
  - Loftus & Loftus 1980: whether forgetting is loss of storage or loss of access "may be impossible to resolve in an absolute sense".
- **Corpus finding**: the Map is split, not silent. [[consciousness-and-memory]] L88 and [[episodic-memory]] L126 take option 1 (brain storage). [[filter-theory]] L75 rejects option 2 on engram evidence. [[bergson-and-duration]] L90 presents option 2 as aligned with filter theory without that caveat.
- **Ranking for the 3 slots**: veto > dormancy > observer-selection. Serial-order should fold into fusion-void (+1005 headroom). Grammar, contingency, perceptual-history and prevalence should fold.
- **Verification**: 15 new citations, every DOI checked at Crossref (Constantinidis et al. 2018 full seven-author list confirmed). Raw texts were grep-verified: Locke (Gutenberg #10615), Broad (archive.org scan, page heads), Leibniz (Bennett's paraphrastic EMT version, flagged), and Joyce's opening pages. Eccles ch. E8 is metadata only. ⚠️ A sentence circulating as Eccles's ("The mind searches the brain's store of engrammed information…") is Custance's unquoted paraphrase. WebFetch mis-attributed it to Popper & Eccles p. 559, and the raw page shows otherwise.
- **For the driver**:
  - (1) `task_chains.pending_articles` holds grammar and observer-selection as its only voids entries. Veto and dormancy are absent, so replenish would spend slots on grammar (a fold) before the top two. This is an operator call under the open voids-slot NEEDS-HUMAN, and was not edited here.
  - (2) Side finding, unminted: [[bergson-and-duration]] L90 ("This aligns with filter theory") lacks [[filter-theory]] L75's engram caveat. A one-clause fix would close it; headroom is 1137 words.

Minting a sixth candidate would repeat the net-negative LIFO move the 10-08 and 10-09 entries declined, so this run worked the triage's own "What would change the ranking" items for veto instead.
- **Key finding**: the veto stays first, and its weak joint is repaired by **bypass**. Every intentional-inhibition paradigm read has to turn the veto into something else before it can observe it: a delay (Filevich et al. 2013 [raw]: the field struggles "largely because of the absence of behavioural markers of inhibition"), a statistical dip with no per-trial record (Matsuhashi & Hallett 2008), a labelled omission (Schel et al. 2014 [raw]) or an external cue (Schultze-Kraft 2016). A new first-person limb: when no action follows, intention reports fall from 35.2% to 16.0% (Schultze-Kraft et al. 2020; n=16; figures summariser-graded ×2). So cancelling an impulse also erodes the subject's own evidence that the impulse existed.
- **Triage decision-changer resolved**: the Schultze-Kraft 2016 main text reports **no** felt point of no return. Its questionnaire covered strategy only, and the SI was not obtainable. Face 3 stands as *unmeasured*, and Matsuhashi 2008 and Parés-Pujolràs 2019 narrow it: preparation is partly felt online, while no felt signal of the *deadline* has been reported. Clinical limb: urge intensity does not predict tic-suppression ability (Ganos et al. 2012), and children suppress tics without reporting urges (Banaschewski et al. 2003).
- **Closed flag**: in the Schultze-Kraft body, "ballistic" names the hypothesis the paper argues *against* (De Jong et al. 1990; Logan & Cowan 1984), which confirms the 10-06 fixes. The paper's PMC ref. 24 attaches the 2014 DOI to Logan & Cowan 1984, so do not copy it.
- **Side finding (unminted, for the driver)**: `topics/bandwidth-of-consciousness` L189 ("before which conscious intervention can veto prepared actions") and `topics/quantum-neural-timing-constraints` L101 ("consciousness can cancel movement onset…") leave out that Schultze-Kraft's stops were cued by an external red light, and the authors write "the original interpretation of the veto was dualistic, whereas in our case veto is meant akin to 'cancellation'". `concepts/libet-experiments` L91 already says "at least for cued stops". ## 20:28 - research-topic
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: Zeno dynamics on a decohered mixture
- **Output**: [[research/zeno-dynamics-on-a-decohered-mixture-2026-10-05]]
- **Sources consulted**: 16 (9 arXiv full texts grep-verified; Home & Whitaker 1997, Joos 1984, Joos & Zeh 1985 and both Laskey 2018 papers at metadata/abstract level only)
- **Finding**: standard Zeno theory holds for mixed states and multi-dimensional projectors (confinement, not freezing) and is an unconditional, non-selective effect, so Stapp's "makes no difference at all" is right about the state. It operates only inside the quadratic window; once the environment resolves inside from outside the leak is a rate and repeated projection changes nothing (Kiefer & Joos), which is Georgiev's redundancy regime. ## 08:27 - research-topic
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: Anticipatory feeling and time preference: is the felt currency hyperbolic?
- **Output**: [[research/anticipatory-feeling-and-time-preference-2026-10-05]]
- **Task**: harvested from `reviews/optimistic-2026-10-04-agency-and-akrasia-wing.md` (New Article Subject 1); target `topics/`, intended slug `anticipatory-feeling-and-time-preference`.
- **Sources consulted**: 17 cited. 8 read as raw artefacts (Loewenstein 1987 and 1996, Story et al. 2013, Berns et al. 2006, Harris 2012 in full; Ainslie 2017, Iigaya et al. 2016, Kim & Zauberman 2009 in part); 9 abstract-only. 6 web searches.
- **Headline finding**: the test the-divided-will sets ("independently shown to be hyperbolic") has never been run. No study fits functional forms to a felt anticipatory measure. The models assume exponential rise (Loewenstein 1987; Story 2013) or constant dread (Berns 2006), and Story et al. set the hyperbolic form aside in so many words, saying the dread-augmented function depends "little on the precise shape of the basic discounting function".
- **The test is also mis-specified**: reversal needs non-stationarity, and a proximity-weighted anticipation term supplies it with exponential components. Loewenstein derives "reverse time inconsistency"; Harris (Study 4, N = 193, hypothetical shocks) reports a dread-driven reversal as the modal pattern (76% of the 103 who took 40 V now over 36 V in a week reversed with 24 weeks interposed), with the classic hyperbolic-direction reversal at 6%.
- **Split verdict for the Map**: on aversive outcomes a felt currency derives expedited pain, which hyperbolic outcome valuation only accommodates. On appetitive outcomes savouring favours delay, so the akratic reversal must come from impatience or visceral craving (Loewenstein 1996; Hardisty & Weber 2020), with no measured curve. The favourable asymmetry attaches to a felt currency and gives nothing to a unitary selector; Iigaya et al. (2020) put anticipatory utility in vmPFC.
- **Quote verification**: every quotation marked verbatim was script-matched against the raw text (62 quoted strings checked; the unmatched ones are abstract quotations checked against API output, plus one Harris range that was cut back because the PDF text layer has an unreadable glyph before the lower bound). Loewenstein 1987 quotations are whitespace-normalised from an OCR layer and flagged as such.
- **Task-lead correction**: the "2004 reprint" doi 10.1515/9781400829118-029 is the 1996 OBHDP paper (65(3), 272–292, doi 10.1006/obhd.1996.0028) reprinted as ch. 26 of *Advances in Behavioral Economics*; the 1996 original was the one read.
- **Not reached**: Frederick et al. 2002 and Loewenstein et al. 2001 beyond abstracts (image-only scans); Hardisty & Weber full text; the philosophical time-bias literature; any cue-versus-delay experiment testing Loewenstein's 1996 contrast. All listed in the note's Gaps section.
- **Chain**: `task_chains.pending_articles` entry added (target_section topics). Suggested follow-up beyond the expand-topic: a one-sentence correction to the-divided-will §accommodation.

- **Headline finding — the rival does not exist in print.** The reviewer framed OSR as "the one live position that agrees with Galileo's exclusion and then denies there was ever anything excluded". Philosophically right, bibliographically wrong. **Raw-artefact keyword census** (curl + Python grep of the fetched HTML, not a summariser): SEP *Structural Realism* — written by Ladyman himself, rev. 2023-05-18, ~170,502 chars — contains **0** occurrences of "consciousness", "conscious" and "experience", and **1** of "qualia", that one being a citation of Unger (1979) for the view that *qualia are the non-structural components of reality*. Mirror-image: SEP *Russellian Monism* has **96** "consciousness" and **0** each of "French", "Esfeld", "relations without relata". The two literatures are effectively disjoint. The composite rival must be assembled from OSR-about-physics (Ladyman & Ross) plus structuralism-about-qualia (Loorits 2014; Fink/Kob/Lyre 2021; Lyre 2022) — and **both phenomenal structuralists decline the ontic reading**: Lyre, verbatim, "One might be inclined to ask whether neurophenomenal structuralism is a version of structural realism. Chalmers is more generous to that rival than the Map is, calling these views "respectable".
- **Third finding — it bites the route, not the thesis.** Eliminative OSR would establish that *physical* entities lack intrinsic natures, not that *experiences* do. It removes `physical-completeness`'s ontological-remainder argument; it does not touch Dualism. An article aiming it at Dualism will have mis-aimed.

Raw grep of the Amherst Lecture PDF (pdftotext of the publisher's own file): **zero** occurrences of "Ladyman" anywhere in it. The parenthesis is Alter and Pereboom's gloss, not Chalmers's citation, and must be attributed accordingly.
